screening_decisions.reason: Cross-sectional survey study, not an RCT/cluster-RCT/quasi-randomised trial. No intervention package evaluated, only preferences assessed.
Before-after study design without randomization. No control group comparison. Not an RCT/cluster-RCT/quasi-randomised trial.

Cluster RCT but intervention is facility-based (job aids for health workers in antenatal clinics), not a community-based intervention package. Outcomes are process measures (counseling quality, knowledge) not mortality/morbidity.
Systematic review, not a primary RCT/cluster-RCT/quasi-randomised trial. Focuses on child mortality from malaria/pneumonia/diarrhoea, not maternal/neonatal outcomes.

RCT but evaluates single intervention (postnatal health education), not a community-based intervention package. Outcomes are infant care practices and family planning, not maternal/neonatal mortality.
Systematic review of intervention packages, not a primary RCT/cluster-RCT/quasi-randomised trial.

RCT but evaluates single intervention (postnatal support worker visits), not a community-based intervention package. Outcomes are maternal mental health and breastfeeding, not maternal/neonatal mortality.

Cluster RCT evaluating community-based participatory women's groups intervention. Primary outcome is neonatal mortality. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, community-based intervention, neonatal mortality outcome.

Cluster RCT evaluating community-based health promotion by Lady Health Workers. Intervention includes multiple components (antenatal and postnatal visits, safe practices education). Outcomes include maternal and neonatal health practices. Uncertain if this constitutes a 'package' - include for further review.

Abstract describes intervention and control areas but design is unclear. May be quasi-experimental. Evaluates antenatal and postnatal care measures for maternal mortality. Include for further review to confirm study design.

RCT but intervention focuses on child development and parenting, not maternal/neonatal mortality or morbidity. Outcomes are immunization, child development, maternal wellbeing - not the review's primary outcomes.
Protocol paper only, no results reported. Outcomes are maternal depression and physical health problems, not maternal/neonatal mortality.

Process evaluation from a cluster RCT of maternal-neonatal health care package. While this paper focuses on surveillance and referral compliance, it is part of a larger trial evaluating a community-based intervention package for neonatal outcomes. Include for further review.
Unclear study design (pre-post with control group, not randomized). Single intervention (antenatal education), not a package. Outcomes are health behaviors, not mortality.

Quasi-experimental design evaluating skilled care initiative (community-based component) on pregnancy-related mortality. Meets criteria: quasi-randomised design, community-based intervention, maternal mortality outcome.

Cluster RCT evaluating community-based prenatal care intervention package (midwife training, community education, equipment). Outcomes include perinatal outcomes. Meets selection criteria despite implementation challenges.
Commentary/opinion piece, not a primary RCT/cluster-RCT/quasi-randomised trial.
Cluster RCT evaluating community-based women's groups intervention. Outcomes include perinatal mortality, stillbirth, neonatal mortality. Meets all selection criteria.
Cluster RCT but evaluates redesigned postnatal care (single intervention), not a community-based intervention package. Outcomes are maternal mental health, not maternal/neonatal mortality.

Quasi-experimental design evaluating community-based integrated nutrition and health programme with maternal-neonatal health component. Primary outcome is neonatal mortality. Meets selection criteria.

This is a cost-effectiveness analysis conducted alongside a cluster-randomised trial, not the primary trial itself. The study focuses on economic evaluation rather than effectiveness of the intervention package.
Cross-sectional survey design, not a randomised, cluster-randomised, or quasi-randomised trial. No randomization was performed.
Review article summarizing evidence on demand-side barriers, not a primary trial. No intervention was evaluated.

Randomized controlled trial of a community-based home visitation intervention by public health nurses. Evaluates infant health outcomes (hospitalizations, emergency room visits) and maternal outcomes (repeat pregnancies). Meets all selection criteria.

Cluster randomised controlled trial of community-based midwife-led postnatal care intervention. Evaluates maternal physical and psychological health outcomes including depression scores. Meets all selection criteria.

While this is a randomized controlled trial of a community-based intervention, the outcomes measured are healthcare utilization behaviors (well-care visits, immunization adherence) rather than maternal/neonatal mortality or morbidity outcomes.
Cluster-randomised controlled trial of community-based women's groups intervention addressing maternal and neonatal care. Primary outcome is neonatal mortality rate. Meets all selection criteria.

Randomised controlled trial of community-based postnatal support interventions. Evaluates maternal and child health outcomes including maternal depression, child injury, and maternal smoking. Meets all selection criteria.
Prospective cohort study examining duration of excess mortality after delivery, not a randomised trial. No intervention was evaluated.
Opinion/commentary article discussing strategic choices for reducing maternal mortality, not a primary research trial.
Policy document outlining Millennium Development Goals, not a primary research trial.
Diagnostic accuracy/validation study comparing CHW assessments to physician gold standard, not a randomised trial evaluating intervention effectiveness.

Contains a cluster-randomized controlled trial component (Neonatal Resuscitation Program) evaluating community-based birth attendant training. Primary outcome is neonatal death in first 7 days. Meets all selection criteria.

Cluster-randomized controlled trial of community-based intervention involving TBA training, safe-delivery kits, and outreach clinics. Primary outcomes are perinatal and maternal mortality. Meets all selection criteria.

Quasi-experimental design evaluating community mobilisation intervention (Skilled Care Initiative). Outcomes include maternal and perinatal mortality. Meets selection criteria as quasi-randomised trial.
Field trial using baseline and endline household surveys without randomization. Appears to be a before-and-after design without control group, not meeting randomisation criteria.
Process paper describing retention strategies and attrition analysis from a trial, not the primary effectiveness trial itself. Does not evaluate intervention effectiveness.
Sub-study/descriptive analysis of referral completion rates from a larger trial, not the primary effectiveness trial. Does not evaluate intervention effectiveness on mortality/morbidity outcomes.
Community-based participatory intervention with triangulated quantitative and qualitative methods, but no randomization. Before-and-after design without control group.

Cluster-randomized controlled trial of community-based maternal and newborn intervention package (CHW home visits, antenatal/postnatal care, referrals). Primary outcomes include neonatal mortality. Meets all selection criteria.
Before-after observational design, not RCT/cluster-RCT/quasi-RCT.
RCT but facility-based education, not community-based package; outcomes are behaviors not mortality.
Descriptive trends analysis, not RCT/cluster-RCT/quasi-RCT.
Cochrane review protocol, not primary trial.
Systematic review, not primary trial.
Cluster-RCT protocol for CHW home-visiting intervention package with multiple components targeting maternal/infant outcomes.
RCT but nursing education program, not community-based; outcomes are attachment/behaviors not mortality.
Observational study, not RCT/cluster-RCT/quasi-RCT.
Before-after surveys, not RCT/cluster-RCT/quasi-RCT.
Protocol for provider-level intervention (steroid kits), not community-based package.
RCT but outcomes are psychosocial (attachment, depression), not mortality/morbidity.
Factorial cluster-RCT evaluating community-based intervention packages with maternal/neonatal/infant mortality as primary outcomes.
Pilot study with matched comparison, not RCT; outcomes are psychosocial not mortality.
Cluster-RCT of home-visits intervention by community volunteers with neonatal mortality as primary outcome.
Cluster-RCT of participatory women's groups addressing maternal/newborn health with neonatal mortality as primary outcome.
Secondary analysis of cluster-RCT data on birth attendant training with perinatal/neonatal mortality outcomes.
RCT in UK (developed country), outcomes are depression/injury/smoking, not mortality.
Observational study on woodsmoke exposure and neurodevelopment, not relevant intervention or outcomes.
Cluster-RCT but health financing intervention (P4P), not community-based package; outcomes are service utilization.
Cluster-RCT but single intervention (birth plans), not package; outcomes are service utilization not mortality.

While this is a randomised controlled trial with community-based intervention, the outcomes measured (general health status SF-36, postnatal depression, breastfeeding rates) do not address maternal/neonatal mortality or morbidity as required by the selection criteria.

This study reports baseline prevalence data from the Philani Mentor Mothers Project, not an evaluation of intervention effectiveness. It is a cross-sectional analysis, not a trial evaluating community-based intervention packages.

This is a cluster-randomized controlled trial evaluating a community-based intervention (facilitation of local stakeholder groups) with neonatal mortality as the primary outcome. Meets all selection criteria.
While this is a randomised clinical trial, the intervention is clinic-based (individually tailored counseling sessions in a clinic setting), not community-based as required by the selection criteria.
This is a randomised controlled trial with community-based peer counsellors intervention. Exclusive breastfeeding is a key neonatal outcome. Meets all selection criteria.
This is a community-based cluster randomized controlled trial evaluating Essential Newborn Care training with perinatal mortality as the primary outcome. Meets all selection criteria.
This is a randomised controlled trial with community-based postnatal home visits intervention. Outcomes include maternal postpartum morbidities and infant morbidity. Meets all selection criteria.

This is a community randomized controlled trial with community-based nutrition counselling intervention. Outcomes include exclusive breastfeeding and complementary feeding practices (neonatal/infant outcomes). Meets all selection criteria.
This study compares midwives with lady home visitors but does not appear to be a randomised, cluster-randomised, or quasi-randomised trial. The study design does not meet the selection criteria.

This is a quasi-experimental evaluation of a community-based breastfeeding promotion programme with peer counselling. Breastfeeding is a neonatal outcome. Quasi-randomised trials are included in the selection criteria.

This is a cluster randomised controlled trial with community-based promotion of exclusive breastfeeding. Outcomes include diarrhoeal illness and growth (neonatal/infant morbidity). Meets all selection criteria.
This is a review of 15 TBA- and midwife-based interventions, not a primary randomised, cluster-randomised, or quasi-randomised trial. Does not meet the study design criteria.

While this is a randomised controlled trial with community-based intervention, the primary outcomes (child injury, maternal smoking, maternal depression) do not address maternal/neonatal mortality or morbidity as required by the selection criteria.
This is a randomised trial with community-based home visits for health education. Outcomes include perinatal mortality, infant morbidity, and breastfeeding practices. Meets all selection criteria.

This is a longitudinal study comparing intervention and comparison areas, but does not appear to be a randomised, cluster-randomised, or quasi-randomised trial. The study design does not meet the selection criteria.
This is a cluster randomised controlled study with community-based intervention (training traditional birth attendants). Primary outcome is neonatal mortality. Meets all selection criteria.

This is a cluster-randomised controlled trial with community-based intervention (CBT by community health workers). Outcomes include maternal depression (maternal morbidity) and infant weight/height (neonatal outcomes). Meets all selection criteria.

This is a randomised community intervention trial with antenatal care packages (community-based). Outcomes include preventable maternal morbidity and preventable perinatal morbidity. Meets all selection criteria.
This is an observational study comparing two districts (Ouargaye and Diapaga), not a randomised, cluster-randomised, or quasi-randomised trial. The study design does not meet the selection criteria.

While this is a randomised controlled trial with community-based intervention, the outcomes focus on H1N1 influenza detection and treatment, not maternal/neonatal mortality or morbidity as required by the selection criteria.

This study describes a health promotion programme introduced in 1981 with comparison to control areas, but does not report randomisation. It appears to be a before-after or observational comparison rather than a randomised, cluster-randomised, or quasi-randomised trial as required by the selection criteria.

This is a cluster randomised control trial evaluating a community-based participatory intervention (women's groups) that measured neonatal mortality rate, maternal mortality ratio, and other perinatal outcomes. Meets all selection criteria: randomised design, community-based intervention package, and relevant maternal/neonatal outcomes.

While this study evaluated safe motherhood interventions with a pilot zone and control area, there is no mention of randomisation. The design appears to be quasi-experimental without random allocation, which does not meet the requirement for randomised, cluster-randomised, or quasi-randomised trials.

Although this is a randomised controlled trial with community-based nursing intervention, it focuses specifically on adolescent mothers (narrow population) and primary outcomes include social outcomes like school dropout rates rather than maternal/neonatal mortality and morbidity. The intervention is not a comprehensive community-based package targeting maternal/neonatal mortality reduction.

This is a systematic review article summarizing evidence from multiple studies, not a primary randomised, cluster-randomised, or quasi-randomised trial. Reviews do not meet the study design criteria specified in the protocol.

This is a secondary analysis of an RCT focusing on perinatal depression outcomes, not maternal or neonatal mortality/morbidity. The intervention is CBT-based for depression treatment, not a community-based intervention package designed to reduce maternal/neonatal mortality.

This is an analytical/modeling paper discussing intervention packages and their potential impact, not a primary randomised, cluster-randomised, or quasi-randomised trial. It does not present trial data meeting the study design criteria.

While this mentions a randomised controlled study with community-based antenatal education, the primary outcomes measured are reproductive health knowledge, attitudes, and behaviors—not maternal or neonatal mortality and morbidity. The outcomes do not align with the review's focus on mortality/morbidity reduction.

This is a two-by-two factorial cluster randomized controlled trial evaluating a community intervention (participatory women's groups) combined with facility quality improvement. Primary outcomes include maternal, perinatal, and neonatal mortality. Meets all selection criteria: randomised design, community-based intervention component, and relevant maternal/neonatal outcomes.

This study describes a peer-counseling intervention with a control area comparison, but there is no indication of randomisation. Additionally, the primary outcome is exclusive breastfeeding rates, not maternal or neonatal mortality/morbidity. Does not meet study design or outcome criteria.

This is a 7-year follow-up of an original RCT, not the primary trial itself. The outcomes measured are child health, nutrition, cognitive stimulation, and parenting skills—not maternal or neonatal mortality and morbidity. The intervention also targets parenting support rather than maternal/neonatal mortality reduction.

This study used a before-after comparison design to evaluate a community organization intervention. There is no mention of randomisation, making it ineligible under the selection criteria requiring randomised, cluster-randomised, or quasi-randomised trials.

This is a cluster randomised controlled trial evaluating the IMNCI programme which includes community-based components (postnatal home visits, women's group meetings). Primary outcomes include neonatal and infant mortality. Meets all selection criteria: randomised design, community-based intervention package, and relevant neonatal outcomes.

This is a cluster-randomised trial evaluating a community-based intervention (SMART Dai training for traditional birth attendants). The study measured maternal and newborn care outcomes and reported significant reduction in perinatal mortality. Meets selection criteria: randomised design, community-based intervention, and relevant maternal/neonatal outcomes.

This is a cluster-randomised controlled efficacy trial evaluating a community-based preventive package of interventions for essential newborn care (birth preparedness, clean delivery, thermal care, breastfeeding promotion, danger sign recognition). Primary outcome was neonatal mortality rate. Meets all selection criteria: randomised design, community-based intervention package, and relevant neonatal mortality outcome.
